sentences.l2: 除夕这天，天还没黑，一家人就已经围坐在厨房的长桌旁包饺子了。
sentences.l1: On Lunar New Year's Eve, before it had even gone dark, the whole family was already sitting around the long table in the kitchen, making dumplings.

sentences.l2: 奶奶揉面，母亲调馅，父亲擀皮，孩子们负责把那些形状略显笨拙的成品摆进竹筛——分工并不固定，却自有一种默契。
sentences.l1: Grandma kneads the dough, Mother mixes the filling, Father rolls out the wrappers, and the children are responsible for placing the slightly clumsy-looking finished dumplings onto the bamboo tray; the division of labour is not fixed, yet it has a tacit understanding of its own.

sentences.l2: 在北方，年夜饭若少了饺子，便算不得完整；而对许多人来说，包饺子本身就是团圆最具体的模样：几双手在同一张案板上忙碌，话题从旧年的得失延伸到新岁的打算。
sentences.l1: In the north, a New Year's Eve dinner without dumplings is not considered complete; and for many people, making dumplings is itself the most concrete form of family reunion: several pairs of hands busy at the same chopping board, the conversation stretching from the gains and losses of the old year to the plans for the new one.

sentences.l2: 按老规矩，母亲会在其中一只饺子里悄悄裹进一枚洗净的硬币。
sentences.l1: According to the old custom, Mother will quietly wrap a washed coin inside one of the dumplings.

sentences.l2: 谁若咬到，便被视作来年最有福气的人。
sentences.l1: Whoever bites into it is regarded as the most fortunate person in the coming year.

sentences.l2: 这自然只是一种讨好彩头的心理慰藉，硬币本身并无魔力；然而恰恰是这份带着笑意的期许，让一顿寻常的晚饭有了仪式感。
sentences.l1: This is naturally only a psychological comfort of courting good luck, and the coin itself has no magic; yet it is precisely this smiling expectation that gives an ordinary dinner a sense of ritual.

sentences.l2: 人们真正在意的，或许并非财运，而是全家人能再一次围坐在一起，把平安与顺遂的愿望，一并包进那层薄薄的面皮里。
sentences.l1: What people truly care about is perhaps not wealth, but that the whole family can sit around together once more and wrap their wishes for peace and smooth fortune, all together, into that thin layer of dough.
